implication: Parent-subsidiary delisting or stake reduction via exchange-traded OFS uses the statutory OFS framework under SEBI ICDR Regulations; the two-tranche (HNI/QIB + retail) structure is standard for listed equity sales but signals potential strategic exit or capital restructuring in the industrial/HVAC space.

framework.ref: SEBI ICDR Regulations 2018, Chapter V (Offer for Sale)
framework.note: central - governs the conduct, eligibility, pricing, and bidding process for OFS by shareholders of listed companies.

framework.ref: SEBI ICDR Regulations 2018, Regulation 2.1(c) (Definition and Categories of Investors)
framework.note: central - defines QIB, HNI and retail investor classes for bifurcated OFS bidding windows.

framework.ref: Listing Regulations 2015 (SEBI), Chapter V (Buyback and OFS)
framework.note: central - prescribes continuous disclosure, timing, and shareholder / exchange notification obligations during OFS.

framework.ref: Companies Act 2013, Section 62 (Authority to Make Further Issue)
framework.note: procedural - secondary transaction does not require fresh authorization; filing of notice with Registrar under Section 42 is required if applicable.

framework.ref: Foreign Exchange Management Act 1999 (FEMA) / Liberalized Remittance Scheme
framework.note: conditional - applies only if foreign shareholders participate or if seller is non-resident; not triggered if domestic parents sell.

framework.ref: National Stock Exchange / BSE Circulars on OFS Mechanism
framework.note: procedural - governs settlement, reporting, RHP validity, and exchange-specific eligibility criteria for the OFS.

framework.ref: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code 2016, Section 29A (Eligibility of Resolution Applicants)
framework.note: conditional - relevant only if seller is in distress; not applicable here.

framework.ref: Income Tax Act 1961, Chapter VI-A (Capital Gains)
framework.note: procedural - seller liable for capital gains tax on sale; TDS may apply depending on buyer identity.

parties: Bosch Global Software Technologies Private Limited (seller); Bosch Home Comfort India Limited (issuer)
headline: Bosch Global Software Technologies announces offer for sale of 19,63,994 shares in Bosch Home Comfort India Limited
sum: Bosch Global Software Technologies launches an OFS of ~19.64 lakh shares in its listed subsidiary Bosch Home Comfort India Limited via stock exchange mechanism, with non-retail bidding on 18 June 2026 and retail bidding on 19 June 2026.
detail: Bosch Global Software Technologies Private Limited, the parent entity, initiated an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 19,63,994 equity shares (face value ₹10 each) in its subsidiary Bosch Home Comfort India Limited through the stock exchange mechanism. The OFS was bifurcated into two phases: non-retail investors (QIB and HNI) on 18 June 2026 (09:15–15:30 hrs) and retail investors on 19 June 2026 (09:15–15:30 hrs). The sale was conducted via BSE/NSE electronic bidding, subject to SEBI oversight and exchange eligibility rules. This transaction represents a secondary market share transfer and does not involve new capital issuance.
